title: The price card that lost its tokens
scenario:
You are the product designer at a small savings app. A developer built the new price card with an AI assistant. The card looks close, but the code has hard-coded colours, odd spacing and a new button instead of the shared one.

Use the exhibit. The tool names are from Figma's tool list. The app, the file and the log are made up for this case.
exhibit:
WHAT THE DEVELOPER SENT (made up)
  A PNG screenshot of the pricing page, pasted into the chat.
  Prompt: "Build this card in React."

WHAT CAME BACK (made up)
  color: #1F7A4D        (the file uses the variable brand/green-600)
  padding: 14px         (the file uses the variable space/16)
  <button className="green-btn">   (the file uses the Button component)

THE FIGMA FILE TODAY (made up)
  Page "Pricing": 1 frame, 240 layers
  Layer names: Frame1268, Group5, Rectangle 12
  Two fills are raw hex, not variables

READ TOOLS ON THE DESIGN SERVER (from Figma's tool list)
  get_design_context   Design context for a layer or selection
  get_metadata         Sparse XML outline of a selection
  get_variable_defs    Variables and styles used in a selection
  get_screenshot       Screenshot of a selection

questions.prompt: Why did the code get #1F7A4D and not the brand/green-600 variable?

options.text: The model drops variable names on purpose, because short hex codes make the code smaller
options.explanation: No vendor page says this. The model never saw the variable name in the first place.

options.text: A screenshot holds only pixels, so the variable name never reached the model at all
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's vision page says the model doesn't process file names or metadata. The token name lives in the file, not in the picture.

options.text: The design context tool always returns hex codes, and it cannot return any token names
options.explanation: The developer never called a design tool. And Figma has get_variable_defs to return variables and styles.

options.text: The PNG was too small to show colour, so the model had to make up a random green
options.explanation: The green is close, so the colour was visible. What was missing is the name behind the colour.

questions.prompt: You want the developer to get the real colour and spacing tokens for the card. Which call fits best?

options.text: get_screenshot of the card again, at a larger size, so the model can read the colours better
options.explanation: A bigger picture still has no token names. Figma uses the screenshot for layout fidelity, next to the structured context.

options.text: get_metadata of the whole page, because the outline lists every colour token in the file
options.explanation: Figma says metadata holds basic properties such as IDs, names, types, position and sizes. It is an outline, not a token list.

options.text: get_variable_defs on the card, with a prompt that asks for the variable names and values
options.explanation: Right. Figma says this tool returns the variables and styles used in a selection, and it suggests naming what you want in the prompt.

options.text: Paste the brand guide PDF into the chat, so the model can match each hex to a name later
options.explanation: That asks the model to guess a match from a picture again. The file already holds the exact names.

questions.prompt: The developer selects the whole Pricing page (240 layers). The answer comes back cut off. What is the best next step?

options.text: Try the same full-page request again later, when the server is less busy and faster
options.explanation: Figma says large selections can cause errors or incomplete responses. The size is the problem, not the time.

options.text: Turn off get_screenshot, because the picture is what makes every response too long
options.explanation: Figma says to turn the screenshot off only for token limits. The selection is still far too large.

options.text: Ask the model to guess the missing part, since the first half of the page looks fine
options.explanation: A guess is how the hex codes got in. Missing context means missing structure.

options.text: Get the metadata outline first, then ask for design context one small part at a time
options.explanation: Right. Figma says to work on smaller sections or components, and to use the outline to break a large design down.

questions.prompt: Which change to the Figma file helps the most before the next handoff?

options.text: Use components, variables for every fill and space, and clear names like PriceCard
options.explanation: Right. Figma's file checklist asks for components, variables and intent-driven names, so the assistant knows what each part is.

options.text: Export one large, sharp screenshot of the page and pin it to the top of the file
options.explanation: A sharper picture still has no names. The vision pages say images may be resized and spatial detail is weak.

options.text: Flatten the card into one image layer, so the model sees a single clean shape
options.explanation: This removes the structure the tools read. The assistant then has even less to work with.

options.text: Write a long chat message that lists every colour and every space by hand
options.explanation: A hand-typed list goes stale and can be wrong. The variables in the file are the source of truth.
